evidence: Caption on page 147 renders '~1.32M tokens' (pdftotext p147 and vision both read 1.32M, not 132M); 436 GB / 0.33 MB = 1.32M, so caption and arithmetic agree. The lead's '100x error' is a decimal-point misread.

Legend on page 147 reads 'full-MHA FP16 (bound, ~2.62 MB/tok)' / 'full-MHA FP8 (raw byte-halving, 50%)' / 'GQA FP16 (~0.33 MB/tok)' / 'GQA FP8 (raw, ~0.16 MB/tok)'. Only one FP16 series per geometry; the orange series is already labelled FP8.

Both callouts use the same operator: '9.5K ≈ 24.9 GB (FP16 bound)' and '9.5K ≈ 3.1 GB (GQA FP16)' (verified by zoomed crop). No 'x' or '=' mismatch exists; the values 24.9 and 3.1 match 2.62/0.33 MB per token at 9.5K.

Text layer (p148) prints 'QLoRA: 4-bit (NF4) base 35 GB + KV 24 GB + LoRA adapters/optimizer ~1 GB' and the bar label '~60 GB'; 35+24+1=60 closes. 24 GB is the canonical 9.2K figure (9,200 x 2.62 MB = 24.1 GB), which the caption itself names ('max 9.5K - canonical input 9.2K'), so the 0.9 GB delta is a context-per-scenario choice, not an arithmetic slip.

Page 148 shows three grey/green reference rules as dashed, dash-dot and dotted, all legible in the white gaps between bars; the levels are additionally restated in the annotations ('~5 GB over 2xH100', 'exceeds an 8xH100 host', 'QLoRA fits a single H100'), so grayscale readers have redundant encoding. Direct right-edge labels would be an improvement, not a defect.

Zoomed crops of page 148 show the styles match the legend: 640 GB rule = dash-dot (as legend's '8xH100 (640 GB)'), 160 GB rule = dashed, 80 GB rule = dotted. Text layer confirms the three legend rows in that order; no swapped styles are rendered.

The 80 GB dotted rule is drawn across the full plot width and is visible in the inter-bar gaps and over the red bar on page 148, so the '1xH100 (80 GB)' legend entry has a referent; the claim that no rule is discernible at 80 GB is not supported by the render.

Pixel analysis of page 149 (orange band x 488-1051, 563 px for 436 GB) finds 17 light vertical dividers at 32.2 px spacing = 24.9 GB per slot, i.e. they exist and are correctly placed, but they are only ~2 px wide and much dimmer than the white dots; the caption itself calls them 'faint', so the subdued treatment is deliberate (a contrast bump would still help at print size).

The dividers are a separate encoding, not the dot grid: 17 continuous light lines at 32.2 px period over a 6 px dot lattice, so the band does not read as a uniform dotted rectangle and the slots can be counted (17 full slots + half slot = 17.5).
Vertical slot rules are present at 24.9 GB spacing inside the orange band (17 lines, 32.2 px apart, measured on page_149.png), contradicting 'no vertical lines at 24.9 GB spacing are visible'.

Text layer (p149) extracts '≈ 436 GB ÷ 24.9 GB ≈ 17.5' and the page image shows a dotted divider sign between the two GB values, matching the line above ('in-flight ≈ KV budget ÷ KV per request') and 436/24.9 = 17.51. No '+' is rendered.

Caption (p151) says the KV block is 'consuming the fixed ~436 GB KV budget', and the same sentence immediately quantifies 436/84 = 5.2 -> 5 and 436/335 = 1.30 -> 1, so the budget is presented as the bound the KV block draws on rather than as fully consumed at 128K. Loose wording, self-corrected in place.

Page 151 carries the annotation '(light rules = 80 GB rank boundaries)' above the plot and the caption's '80 GB rank-boundary lines' has a referent; the light horizontal rules are drawn at 80 GB intervals (text layer + image).

The note on page 151 actually reads 'Bar heights are to scale (GB)' (pdftotext and vision agree), the opposite of what the lead quotes; bar tops land on the 80 GB rules at 229/288/539 GB, consistent with the labelled totals.

Title 'Memory Tetris: how the 8xH100 host (640 GB) fills with context' describes the filling process the three bars depict (229 -> 288 -> 539 GB against the 640 GB rule) without claiming saturation; 'fills with context' is a legitimate process description, with the ceiling rule drawn explicitly.
